title: Directory and authorization details
rows: AD DS / AD FS
AD DS provides a directory/domain. AD FS federates authentication; it does not replace a domain controller.
Managed Microsoft AD
Managed domain controllers across two AZs; supported trusts, integrations, sharing and multi-Region replication have separate prerequisites.
AD Connector / Simple AD
Connector proxies supported requests to an existing directory. Simple AD is a limited Samba-compatible directory, with no forest trusts or MFA support.
Policy attachment
AWS-managed and customer-managed policies are reusable; inline policies belong to one identity. Inspect current AWS-managed policy versions.
ForAllValues / ForAnyValue
Compare supplied values of multivalued request keys. ForAllValues can match a missing key; use Null/presence checks and separate required-tag conditions.
STS sessions
AssumeRole, AssumeRoleWithSAML, AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity, GetSessionToken and GetFederationToken create different session types. Trust, caller authorization and session restrictions differ.

title: Organization setup and policy boundaries
rows: Created / invited accounts
Organizations normally creates OrganizationAccountAccessRole for a created member account. Invitation does not automatically create that role.
Account moves
Meet removal prerequisites, leave/remove the old organization, then invite and accept into the new one. Recheck effective policies, service integrations and billing.
Feature modes
Consolidated billing aggregates usage/payment. All features adds governance; enabling it can require invited-account approval and cannot be downgraded to billing-only.
Discount sharing
Eligible RI/Savings Plans sharing is controlled through billing settings. It does not grant resource access or automatically share capacity reservations.
Tag policy
Supported key/value/capitalization enforcement is different from requiring every tag to exist. Use supported request-tag/provisioning controls for mandatory presence.
AI opt-out / backup policy
AI opt-out applies to eligible service data use. Backup policies express organization intent; verify assignments, successful jobs, retention and tested restores.

title: Parameter, secret and key details
rows: Parameter Store Standard
10,000 parameters per account/Region; values up to 4 KB. Standard parameters do not support advanced parameter policies or cross-account sharing.
Parameter Store Advanced
100,000 parameters per account/Region; values up to 8 KB. Supports parameter policies and supported cross-account sharing; additional charges apply. An advanced parameter cannot be downgraded.
Policies / throughput
Expiration deletes the parameter; ExpirationNotification and NoChangeNotification emit notifications. Storage tier and throughput settings are separate decisions.
Recursive paths
An allowed recursive GetParametersByPath parent can expose descendants. Design hierarchy authorization deliberately rather than treating child-path restrictions as a guaranteed boundary.
Secret rotation / CloudFormation
Dynamic references resolve during relevant stack resource operations. Changing a secret alone does not automatically refresh the resource that consumed it.
Cross-account secrets
Align the secret resource policy, caller identity permissions and customer-managed KMS key authorization.
Key custody
AWS KMS key material origin, imported material, CloudHSM custom key stores and external key stores have different custody and availability dependencies.
TLS with CloudHSM
The application server terminates TLS and uses supported HSM-backed private-key operations. CloudHSM is not a transparent traffic proxy.

title: Network controls and diagnostic precision
rows: Security groups
Stateful allow rules at supported resource/ENI scope. They do not create routes.
Network ACLs
Stateless subnet controls; numbered allow/deny rules use first match. Permit return traffic and the actual client ephemeral-port range.
Flow Log fields
Read interface, srcaddr/dstaddr, ports, protocol, counts, start/end, action and log-status. pkt-srcaddr/pkt-dstaddr can preserve original packet addresses across intermediaries.
Diagnostic limits
ACCEPT is not proof of application success; REJECT alone does not identify the complete cause. Excluded traffic, delays and SKIPDATA limit observations.
NAT instance
Configure both route directions, public connectivity, security controls and disabled source/destination checking. Operate capacity, patching and recovery yourself.
Private DNS
Verify VPC DNS settings, endpoint scope, zone conflicts and hybrid Resolver forwarding. DNS resolution, connectivity and authorization are separate checks.

title: DNS routing and health details
rows: IP-based routing
Uses configured source CIDR collections; account for recursive resolver behavior and EDNS Client Subnet support.
Geolocation / geoproximity
Geolocation uses geographic policy; geoproximity uses resource location and bias. Current geoproximity records can be managed directly; Traffic Flow is not universally mandatory.
Weighted records
Weights influence eligible DNS answers, not an exact percentage of HTTP requests. Resolver/client caching, TTLs and health affect observed traffic.
Endpoint health
HTTP/HTTPS checks evaluate supported response status and optional string matching in the first 5,120 response bytes. Route 53 global checker aggregation differs from one probe result.
Private endpoints
Public Route 53 checkers cannot directly probe arbitrary private addresses; use appropriate CloudWatch-alarm or calculated health designs.
Calculated checks

AWS documentation describes child-check limits differently across overview and console pages (255/256). Check the current API/console constraint for the operation instead of assuming interchangeability.
Traffic Flow
Policies and policy records are versioned configuration. A policy change and DNS cache expiry are separate events.

title: S3 access and legacy feature boundaries
rows: Multi-Region Access Points
A global access/routing endpoint does not automatically replicate bucket data. Configure replication and test failover independently.
Presigned URLs
They carry the signing principal's permitted operation. They expire no later than the underlying credentials and remain subject to applicable policy restrictions.
Object Lambda
Since 7 November 2025, availability is restricted to existing customers and selected APN partners. Treat older PDF designs as eligibility-dependent.
Glacier Vault Lock
A legacy Glacier vault policy lock is different from S3 Object Lock and from using an S3 Glacier storage class.
Observability
Server access logs, CloudTrail data events and CloudWatch metrics answer different questions; configuration does not prove complete event capture.

title: EBS volume limits and comparison
rows: gp3
1 GiB–64 TiB; up to 80,000 IOPS and 2,000 MiB/s. Includes 3,000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s baseline; provisioning ratios, instance limits and platform constraints apply.
gp2
1 GiB–16 TiB; up to 16,000 IOPS and 250 MiB/s. Performance and burst behavior depend on size.
io2 Block Express
4 GiB–64 TiB; up to 256,000 IOPS and 4,000 MiB/s on compatible instances/configurations; designed for 99.999% durability.
io1
4 GiB–16 TiB; up to 64,000 IOPS and 1,000 MiB/s under supported instance/configuration conditions.
st1 / sc1
125 GiB–16 TiB; up to 500/250 MiB/s and 500/250 IOPS at 1 MiB I/O respectively. Throughput-oriented HDD; cannot be boot volumes.
Multi-Attach
Supported io1/io2 volumes: up to 16 Nitro instances in one AZ. Linux supports io1/io2; Windows supports io2. Coordinate concurrent writes with a suitable application/filesystem.
Scope exceptions
Outposts gp3 limits differ from regional gp3. The PDF's 7.5/60 TiB instance-store examples describe particular instance configurations, not a universal current limit.
Instance store lifecycle
Host-local block storage survives a normal reboot, but data is lost on stop/termination and can be lost on host failure. Capacity cannot be expanded like EBS; operate independent backups.

title: Snapshot recovery and EFS details
rows: Capture consistency
Detachment is optional. Quiesce the application and flush pending writes; coordinate related volumes. A crash-consistent block capture is not automatically application-consistent.
Fast Snapshot Restore

Enable per snapshot/AZ and account for additional charges and volume-creation credits. Snapshot size is limited to 16 TiB; full performance benefits have documented 64,000 IOPS / 1,000 MiB/s boundaries.
Provisioned initialization
Choose 100–300 MiB/s where supported. Initialization concerns snapshot data size, not simply allocated volume size. Specifying a rate takes precedence over FSR.
Manual initialization
Read every required block safely using a supported read-only method such as fio/dd to /dev/null. Do not overwrite the restored device.
EFS bursting
Baseline is 50 MiB/s per TiB of Standard storage, with a minimum baseline. Burst credits and capacity determine burst performance; read requests are metered at one-third the write rate.
EFS access controls
Network reachability, IAM client permissions and POSIX permissions are separate gates. Access points can enforce a root directory and UID/GID; they do not bypass missing permissions.
Default EFS policy
Without a user-configured filesystem policy, the default allows anonymous network-reachable clients, subject to POSIX permissions. Use the mount helper and supported IAM authorization deliberately.
EFS replication
Initial synchronization precedes destination availability. Most filesystems target a 15-minute RPO; high-churn very large filesystems/files can exceed it. Monitor TimeSinceLastSync and test RTO.
Current performance
Regional Elastic throughput limits vary by Region and supported client. Older universal ceilings in the PDF are historical; check the current performance table for the selected configuration.
EFS protocol and scale
Managed NFSv4.0/v4.1 with POSIX semantics; scalable to petabytes and thousands of concurrent clients. Linux file workloads differ from native Windows SMB.
Performance modes
General Purpose is recommended for low latency. Max I/O is a creation-time choice, has higher per-operation latency, and is unavailable for One Zone filesystems or Elastic throughput.
Storage class eligibility

Regional supports Standard, IA and Archive; One Zone supports One Zone and One Zone-IA, with automatic backups enabled by default. Archive requires supported Regional/Elastic configuration. Lifecycle eligibility and minimum storage charges apply.
Hybrid mount paths
Use supported private DX/VPN or peering paths, NFS TCP 2049, mount-target security groups and correct DNS or explicit target addressing. Design redundant connectivity and mount targets.
Cost comparisons

The PDF’s 3× gp2, 50% Archive and >90% savings figures are scenario/price illustrations, not universal current prices. Compare Region-specific storage, access, retrieval, throughput and minimum-duration charges.
Replication throughput
Replication uses managed capacity rather than consuming the source filesystem’s provisioned throughput allocation. This does not eliminate initial-copy duration, lag or failover work.

title: FSx and Storage Gateway details
rows: FSx for Windows
SMB/NTFS, AD authentication, ACLs, quotas and supported DFS patterns. Distinguish SSD/HDD, backup protection and Single-AZ/Multi-AZ availability.
Lustre scratch
Data is not replicated; failed file servers are not replaced. Scratch can burst up to six times a 200 MBps/TiB baseline. Keep recreatable inputs and valuable outputs independently protected.
Lustre persistent SSD/HDD
Replicates data within one AZ and replaces failed servers. Persistent 1/2 and media choices have different capacity, throughput and deployment constraints.
Lustre Intelligent-Tiering

Current persistent Intelligent-Tiering replicates data across multiple AZs, offers elastic tiered storage and optional SSD read cache. Data durability is distinct from serving availability and application DR.
ONTAP / OpenZFS
ONTAP supports NFS/SMB/iSCSI and storage-management features. OpenZFS serves NFS; do not treat older headline IOPS/latency figures as guarantees for every configuration.
File Gateway disks
S3 File Gateway uses local cache disks. Volume/Tape Gateway upload buffers are separate type-specific concepts; do not apply their disk model to File Gateway.
S3 event workflows
Newly uploaded objects can trigger supported event processing and feed Athena, Redshift Spectrum or EMR. Configure replication separately for a second Region.
Multiple gateways
Prefer one authoritative writer per object set with read-only consumers where appropriate. RefreshCache updates inventory; it does not eagerly download all object bytes.
Recovery and immutability

Lifecycle can reduce storage cost but archive retrieval may require restoration. Recover a previous version deliberately, refresh gateway metadata, and understand Object Lock protects object versions rather than freezing every filename forever.
Volume / Tape Gateway
Volume Gateway recovery uses EBS snapshots with type-specific local storage. Tape Gateway eject/archive and virtual-library recovery are different workflows.
Legacy availability

Storage Gateway hardware appliances stopped new sales in May 2025, with existing support scheduled through May 2028. FSx File Gateway is unavailable to new customers; retain historical context without recommending an ineligible new deployment.
Supported client examples

ONTAP and OpenZFS can serve compatible Linux, Windows and macOS clients, on-premises systems, EC2 and container workloads. VMware, WorkSpaces and application-streaming integrations require supported protocol/client/network configurations.
Gateway deployment

Use a supported VM/host deployment and type-specific CPU, memory, disk and network sizing. The PDF’s hardware-purchase path is historical; private or encrypted internet transport remains a separate design choice.
S3 File Gateway storage classes

Supported active-object destinations include Standard, Standard-IA, One Zone-IA and Intelligent-Tiering. Lifecycle transitions into archive classes change retrieval behavior; confirm current gateway compatibility and restore requirements.
FSx File Gateway historical architecture
The historical service exposed FSx for Windows via SMB with NTFS/AD compatibility and a local hot-data cache, commonly for home directories/group shares. It is closed to new customers.
Lustre repository behavior

Import namespace/metadata and load needed file contents on demand. Retained data can avoid repeated reads, but eviction and configured import/export behavior determine later S3 requests. Supported private connectivity is required for on-premises clients.
